title: Composition and unit equations of normalized strict scalar cone data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ and any scheme map $g:X\to Y$. Use the strict cone data, normalized tensor associators, composition condition and unit condition of [def-sf-scalar-pullback-strict-cone-data]. Every such datum for $E\to L$ satisfies the composition condition for every further finite extension $L\to F$ and every supplied pair of data for $L\to F$ and $E\to F$. Every datum for the identity extension $E\to E$ satisfies the unit condition. These equations concern only the strict tower and the two cone coordinates. The statement does not construct any datum or assert a derived descent or its uniqueness.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary scalar associator and its inverse on local tensors by ((p tensor s) tensor z) maps to p tensor (j(s)z), and p tensor z maps to (p tensor 1) tensor z. The tensor balances and inverse identities hold locally and survive sheafification. These are natural chain isomorphisms with the association normalization. The two completed coefficient maps compose: after every finite projection both composites are the same quotient inclusion; joint monicity of the completed coefficient limit projections proves equality. The identity map is identified in the same way.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; the local construction in Steps 1–3 of lem-weil-scalar-pullback-strict-cone-naturality, from Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 6.5.9(4).

proof.text: For a triple $E\subset L\subset F$, write $j_{LF}:S_{L,X}\to S_{F,X}$ for the completed coefficient map. The same-index quotient maps satisfy $\iota_{LF,m}\iota_{EL,m}=\iota_{EF,m}$, since they all send the class of an integral element to its class in the final quotient. On a generator $(((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s)\otimes t$, the successive level maps give first coordinate $g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_{EF,m}(\bar a))$ and final multiplier $\iota_{EF,m}(b)\pi^F_m(j_{LF}(s))\pi^F_m(t)$. The direct level map after associating the scalar tensors gives the same multiplier $\iota_{EF,m}(b)\pi^F_m(j_{LF}(s)t)$. The target associator on $P\otimes S_L\otimes S_F$ is multiplication on the scalar factors, as in Step 1. Equality on generators and sheafification therefore prove composition of $d_m$. The product comparisons respect these associators: their $m$th projections are all the tensor of $\operatorname{pr}_m$ followed by the same scalar multiplication. Hence the two composite cone maps agree on each of their two coordinates. For $L=E$, $\iota_m$ is the quotient identity and the formula becomes multiplication by $\pi^E_m(s)$, exactly the tensor unitor. The product and cone comparisons then also become their unit identifications.

theorem scalarPullbackStrictCoherence {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}}
    (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    (∀ D : ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E L ι g,
      ScalarPullbackCompositionFormula l E L ι g D) ∧
    (∀ D : ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) g,
      ScalarPullbackUnitFormula l E g D)
